summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male nursing home resident with a history of stroke, tracheostomy, G-tube, atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, diabetes, and recurrent infections was admitted with fever, hypotension, and leukocytosis. He was diagnosed with sepsis likely from a urinary tract infection and possible pneumonia. He was treated with IV fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics, including vancomycin and cefepime. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. His infection markers improved, and he was discharged to extended care with plans to follow up with urology for evaluation of a suprapubic catheter to reduce future UTI risk. His chronic conditions, including neuropathic pain and pressure ulcer, were managed throughout the stay.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
